newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: UIC hits new low in active trade.
newsitem.headline: UIC hits new low in active trade.

text.p: Property company United Industrial Corp (UIC) hit a new year low of Singapore $1.06 on Wednesday afternoon despite a rebound in most property shares.
At 0745 GMT, the shares were trading around S$1.08, down one cent in active volume of more than five million shares.
The property index was however up 5.42 points at 652.38 as fears of new government curbs subsided.
Most analysts said they maintained a "sell" recommendation on UIC as its growth prospects were not exciting.
"UIC has not added any significant investments to its portfolio," Soc-Gen Crosby Securities Pte Ltd said.
Analysts said the company's performance this year was likely to fall below the the property sector's average.
"I am looking for a two percent growth this year compared to the property sector average growth of 12 percent in 1997," said Lim Chung Chun, assistant director at ING Barings Securities.
According to the Edinburgh Financial Publication's The Estimate Directory, UIC's net profit is expected to be around S$73.9 million for financial year ending December 31, 1997.
Last year, UIC saw a 10 percent gain in net profit to Singapore $68.62 million.
But analysts said they were unimpressed as most of the gains were aided by a tax write-back.
They said UIC, which has a high exposure to the office sector, was affected by falling office rentals.
